rationale: PP-OCRv6 CAN emit ASCII space, at token 18709. Tesseract can too. The whitespace-free representation stays primary so this benchmark remains comparable with PR #214, whose Arm B could not emit a space at all; the boundary-preserving representation becomes substantively meaningful for the first time and is reported as a full secondary comparison rather than as a footnote.

steps: convert every Unicode whitespace run to one ASCII space
2_boundaryPreservingNormalized.purpose: Substantively meaningful in this benchmark, because both arms can represent word boundaries.

3_whitespaceFreeComparable.purpose: The primary comparable representation, chosen to preserve comparability with PR #214.

prohibited.note: Every entry is false: none of these transformations is applied to either arm anywhere.

reportingRule: All three representations are reported for every item in both arms. Whitespace-free matching is never described as raw exact matching.
